claim: The Ascon v1.2 NIST submission formally defines the cipher suite covering authenticated encryption (ASCON-128, ASCON-128a), a hash function, and an extendable output function, all built on a common permutation.
stance_target: ground-truth definition of the algorithm family that student FPGA implementations must faithfully reproduce
scope_conditions: official NIST submission specification, version 1.2, May 31 2021
quoted_support: Algorithms in the Ascon Cipher Suite ... Recommended Parameter Sets ... State and Notation ... Authenticated Encryption ... Hashing

claim: The Ascon permutation operates on a 320-bit state and consists of three layers per round: addition of round constants, a nonlinear substitution layer (5x5 S-box), and a linear diffusion layer using fixed bit rotations per 64-bit word.
stance_target: precise algorithmic structure that any Verilog/VHDL implementation (like the ASCON FPGA paper in this batch) must implement bit-exactly
quoted_support: Permutation ... Addition of Constants ... Substitution Layer ... Linear Diffusion Layer

claim: The specification includes formal security claims and bounds for both the authenticated-encryption and hashing modes, plus an explicit design-rationale section justifying round-number and parameter choices for lightweight vs. high-performance use cases.
stance_target: provides the formal security-analysis backbone a student paper needs to argue publishable rigor beyond a bare implementation
scope_conditions: sections 3-5 of the NIST submission document
quoted_support: Security Claims ... Authenticated Encryption ... Hashing ... Features ... Features for Lightweight Applications ... Features for High-Performance Applications ... Design Rationale
